subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw keep `timeoutSeconds` as the hard wall-clock ceiling and add a separate activity/idle timeout, or should `timeoutSeconds` itself become activity-aware?
rationale: Both shapes are technically plausible, but the choice changes core runtime semantics, config schema, runaway-resource protection, and how the open partial timeout PRs should be reviewed.

options.title: Add idle budget plus hard cap
options.body: Introduce an explicit liveness/idle budget while preserving a hard maximum run ceiling and a compatibility plan for existing `timeoutSeconds` users.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics and improve UX
options.body: Leave the current hard wall-clock budget unchanged and land only notices/progress improvements so users understand long-turn failures.

options.title: Limit work to narrow slices
options.body: Treat subagent idle watchdogs, Telegram progress previews, and timeout notices as independent fixes and defer the core timeout contract.

recommendation.title: Add idle budget plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Introduce an explicit liveness/idle budget while preserving a hard maximum run ceiling and a compatibility plan for existing `timeoutSeconds` users.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway abort tracking, embedded-runner timeout semantics, and config compatibility, all areas with recent direct history from this owner candidate.
